styleMarkers.rule: The reader is the grammatical subject; abstractions do not act.
Inner states are offered with may, never asserted as diagnosis.
Alternatives are real options, not images; use no metaphor in this register.
Rhythm is even and comma-joined; use no staccato punch sentences.
The word whether is not owner language and must not appear.
Ambient-force energy language is banned; ordinary effort-cost use remains allowed.

dailyRules.rule: Vary sentence structures across the batch; each structural function must sound independently authored.
Keep conjunction saturated, square internally frictional, opposition frictional through another person, soft mildly easier, and house fallback topic-led.
Land the close on the single concrete instruction and keep it literal to the behavior already shown.
Describe a brief available condition or friction at hours scale; results remain open.
Address the reader with respect and treat their ordinary baseline as capable.
When a room appears, use it only as a concrete collective subject in motion.
Give the body a key-specific opener construction that does not repeat another batch opener; today is allowed.
A room may act collectively; audience comparisons must stay attached to a named ordinary behavior.
A single instruction may naturally enumerate one person, one action, or one change without being split into extra instructions.
House fallback copy begins from its life topic, names the pull plainly, and ends at speak-up scale.

batch1LintGuidance.rule: Use at most one time-anchor phrase anywhere in the body, including today and next-few-hours constructions.
Use may only for a reader's inner state, never as padding on observable actions or every clause.
Match the headline grammar of the approved exemplar for this group, not only its topic or tone.
Conjunction has no approved exemplar and must establish saturation without imitating square, opposition, or soft headline grammar.

referencePassages.text: It takes less energy to do the thing than to keep putting it off.

For the next few hours, it is easier to act on what you want instead of just thinking about it. The task, conversation, or decision you have been putting off may still be annoying, but it feels more possible now. Give it thirty minutes before your mind starts making the case for waiting again.
Comfort is a quick substitute for admitting what you actually want.

Pay attention to every trip to the kitchen today, because hunger is rarely the whole story. Before reaching for another snack, put a name on whatever desire you are trying to quiet down, even if it feels inconvenient, disruptive, or unlikely. If food is still what you want after that, enjoy it. Just stop using it to answer questions you are avoiding.
Someone else's pressure can easily bait you into overreacting.

Expect an urge to fire back when someone pushes a boundary or questions your judgment. Their edge can make instantaneous defense feel like self-preservation before you even hear them out. Ask one clear question, let them answer without interruption, and only then decide how much weight to give it.
